newsitem.title: MEXICO: Heatwave in Mexico's Sonora kills off 2,694 cattle.
newsitem.headline: Heatwave in Mexico's Sonora kills off 2,694 cattle.

text.p: A prolonged heatwave in the northwestern Mexican state of Sonora has killed 2,694 head of cattle so far this year, the state news agency Notimex said.

Arnoldo Molina Hernandez, an official with the Sonora government Livestock Development body, told Notimex that in the last week 450 head had been lost to dehydration because of the lack of rain and intense heat.
Molina said the state cattle count was at 1,556,617 head, the lowest in the last five years.
Two years ago, much of Mexico's north was hit by a long-lasting drought that forced many cattlemen to kill their animals rather than watch them die.
